The '''Dhubri-Phulbari Bridge''' is an under-construction four lane extradosed cable stay bridge over the [[Brahmaputra River]] between [[Assam]] and [[Meghalaya]] in [[North-East India]].

The Dhubri-Phulbari bridge, to be completed by 2028, would be India's second longest bridge over water after the [[Mumbai Trans Harbour Link]], and would span more than 19 km. This bridge, close to the Bangladesh border, will connect Assam's [[Dhubri]] with Meghalaya's [[Phulbari Assembly constituency|Phulbari]]. It will fill in a missing link of [[National Highway 127B (India)|National Highway 127B]], connecting Dhubri by road to [[Tura, Meghalaya|Tura]], [[Nongstoin]], and other towns in western and central Meghalaya.<ref name="PIB">{{Cite web |date=28 February 2019 |title=Cabinet approves construction of four lane bridge including approaches over River Brahmaputra between Dhubri (on North Bank, Assam) and Phulbari (On South Bank, Meghalaya) on NH-127B with loan assistance from JICA |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1566784 |access-date=29 June 2025 |website=Press Information Bureau, Government of India}}</ref>

Civil works started in 2019–2020. The project is being funded by [[Japan International Cooperation Agency]], and it would be executed by [[National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited]]. It is one of 6 [[Brahmaputra River#Bridges|proposed bridges]] on the Brahmaputra.<ref>{{Cite news |date=12 November 2020 |title=Larsen & Toubro emerges as L1 to construct the country’s longest road bridge over the Brahmaputra |url=https://www.uniindia.com/larsen-toubro-emerges-as-l1-to-construct-the-country-s-longest-road-bridge-over-the-brahmaputra/east/news/2232687.html |access-date=29 June 2025}}</ref>

== Construction ==
[[Larsen and Toubro]] acquired the construction contract for the project, which will feature a navigation bridge including 12.625 km approach [[viaduct]]s of 3.5 km on the [[Dhubri]] side and 2.2 km on the Phulbari side, connected with approach roads and interchanges on both sides.<ref>https://themetrorailguy.com/dhubri-phulbari-bridge-status-update-news-design/</ref>

The bridge is expected to be built with a total cost of approximately Rs 4,997 [[crore]], will meet the long-standing demand of the people from [[Assam]] and [[Meghalaya]] who have depended on ferry services to travel between the two banks of the river. It will reduce the distance of 205 Km to be travelled by Road to 19 Km, which is the total length of the bridge.<ref name="PIB"/>

==Current status==

By April 2025, Indian media reported about 59% of the work completed. The project remains under active execution by NHIDCL, with supervision from the [[Ministry of Road Transport and Highways|Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways]]. Current plans target final completion and opening around late 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dhubri Phulbari Bridge, Length, Estimated Cost, Latest News |url=https://vajiramandravi.com/current-affairs/dhubri-phulbari-bridge/ |access-date=2025-06-29 |language=en-IN}}</ref>
